narration: So how long will 212 gigabytes really take?

subtitle: 212 GB  ·  HOW LONG IT TAKES::100 MBPS=4.7|600 MBPS=0.75

narration: On a 100 megabit connection, close to five hours.
On 600 megabits, about 45 minutes.
Those are perfect-world numbers, and launch week is never a perfect world, so if your internet is slow, the preload is the only thing that matters.
Digital pre-orders could start preloading on November 10th.
title: checklist
subtitle: FIX 1/THE PRELOAD::STARTED NOVEMBER 10|OPEN GTA 6 IN YOUR LIBRARY|IS THE BAR MOVING?|NOT MOVING? START IT YOURSELF

narration: Open GTA 6 in your library and confirm the progress bar is actually moving.
If it is not, start it yourself.
And if you can, run a cable to the console instead of trusting Wi-Fi.
title: cards
subtitle: CABLE vs WI-FI::ETHERNET=Steady|WI-FI=Don't trust it

narration: That is fix one.
title: FIX 1
subtitle: PRELOAD + CABLE

narration: Fix two is space, and this is where people get caught.
title: FIX 2
subtitle: SPACE

title: stats
subtitle: THE GAP::212 GB=Rockstar|223 GB=data miners  ·  +11

narration: The end of this video shows what some of those gigabytes really are.
Add a likely day-one patch on top and I would want 230 gigabytes free.

narration: If you are short, do not delete a single game yet.
title: DON'T DELETE GAMES
subtitle: CHECK THE CAPTURE GALLERY FIRST

narration: Check your capture gallery first, because trophy clips save themselves automatically, and after a few years they can eat a shocking amount of your drive.
Sort by size, clear the big ones or move them to a USB stick, then switch trophy videos off in the capture settings.
title: FIX 2 · FREE THE SPACE
subtitle: Sort the gallery by size; Clear the big clips; Or move them to a USB stick; Turn trophy videos off

narration: If you still need room, buy an internal SSD, because a USB drive can store PS5 games but it cannot play them.
title: cards
subtitle: PS5 STORAGE::INTERNAL SSD=Stores and plays|USB DRIVE=Stores, can't play

narration: Fix three is to let the console work while you sleep.
title: FIX 3
subtitle: WORK WHILE YOU SLEEP

narration: In the power saving settings, turn on staying connected to the internet in rest mode and keep automatic downloads on.
title: checklist
subtitle: POWER SAVING/REST MODE::STAY CONNECTED TO THE INTERNET|AUTOMATIC DOWNLOADS ON

narration: Do your console and controller updates today as well, so nothing new is waiting for you on launch night.
title: checklist
subtitle: TODAY::CONSOLE UPDATE|CONTROLLER UPDATE

narration: So the download is handled.
But here is the question nobody asks until it is too late.
What happens when the game is installed and it still feels wrong?
That is problem two, the screen.
title: THE SCREEN
subtitle: Problem 2  ·  fixes 4 to 7

narration: On November 10th, Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 targets 30 frames per second on every console, the PS5 Pro included.
title: stats
subtitle: ROCKSTAR · NOV 10::30 FPS=every console|PS5 PRO=included

narration: The Pro gets a sharper image from PSSR, Sony's AI upscaler, plus ray traced shadows you will not see anywhere else.
title: cards
subtitle: PS5 PRO ONLY::PSSR=Sony's AI upscaler|RAY TRACED SHADOWS=Nowhere else

narration: Every PS5 gets haptic feedback across the whole game, Tempest 3D audio, and faster loading.
title: checklist
subtitle: EVERY PS5::HAPTIC FEEDBACK|TEMPEST 3D AUDIO|FASTER LOADING

narration: Thirty frames is fine, but it means any delay your TV adds is easier to feel, and that brings us to fix four.
title: FIX 4
subtitle: GAME MODE

narration: Turn on game mode and turn off motion smoothing.
title: cards
subtitle: YOUR TV::GAME MODE=On|MOTION SMOOTHING=Off

narration: Motion smoothing invents extra frames between the real ones, and to do that it holds your picture back, which is the exact opposite of what you want.
Fix five is checking that you are really getting 4K.
title: FIX 5
subtitle: REAL 4K

narration: On PS5, open screen and video.
title: cards
subtitle: SCREEN AND VIDEO::VIDEO OUTPUT INFO=What the console sends|TV CAPABILITIES=What the TV accepts

narration: One page shows the signal your console is sending, and the other shows what your TV can accept.
If a 4K TV never offers 2160p, something between the two is holding the signal back, most often an old HDMI cable or a soundbar passing it through.
title: checklist
subtitle: NO 2160P? THE USUAL CULPRITS::AN OLD HDMI CABLE|A SOUNDBAR PASSING IT THROUGH

narration: Fix six is the HDR calibration.
title: FIX 6
subtitle: HDR

narration: It takes about a minute, and you just raise each pattern until the symbol barely fades out.
Then leave VRR and 120 hertz on automatic.
title: cards
subtitle: LEAVE ON AUTOMATIC::VRR=Automatic|120 HZ=Automatic

narration: Why would I tell you to keep a 120 hertz setting on for a 30 frame game?
title: 120 HZ?
subtitle: FOR A 30 FPS GAME

narration: Hold that thought, because the answer is waiting in the files.
Fix seven is sound.
title: FIX 7
subtitle: SOUND

title: checklist
subtitle: SOUND SETTINGS::3D AUDIO ON|ANY WIRED HEADPHONES IN THE CONTROLLER

title: cards
subtitle: SOUNDBAR OR SURROUND::OUTPUT=Not stereo

narration: Keep haptics and adaptive triggers on, and if they get tiring, there is a slider in accessibility.
title: controller
subtitle: KEEP THEM ON::R2=ADAPTIVE TRIGGERS|L2=ADAPTIVE TRIGGERS

narration: Then charge the controller and clear the dust from the console's vents before your first long session.
title: checklist
subtitle: BEFORE THE FIRST LONG SESSION::CHARGE THE CONTROLLER|CLEAR THE DUST FROM THE VENTS
